obligationsRepaired.theRuleThatDecides: A conviction cell refused for width is offered ONE second chance at 6pt, and the offer is taken only if the drawn lines concatenate back to the held value exactly AND every line but the last ends at a delimiter of the value itself, so no token is broken across lines. A case number cut after 'SUPPLE' reads as two values; one cut after '2024-0011882-' reads as the number it is. A cell that fails the test keeps the old answer and its row is withheld whole, declared and disclosed. Nothing is shortened, abbreviated or invented, and no value is drawn below the 6pt readable floor.

whatAFreshIndependentReadShouldRuleOn: Whether writing item 1 row a of the boundary record at 6pt on two lines is the right answer, or whether the old answer - withhold the row whole, declare it and disclose it - was better. This lane's position is that a conviction the platform holds, missing from a table a court reads as the whole list, is worse than a smaller two-line entry that carries the value whole; and that the delimiter rule, not the size, is what makes it legible. It is the single most consequential judgement in this repair.

Whether setting the multiline flag on the working copy of a field the issuer flagged single-line is acceptable, given that the cell is an open box 21pt tall with no interior rule and the artifact is flattened. Five Illinois builders in this corpus already do the same thing directly, at the same 6pt.

Whether the boundary side, now that it exists, says everything a reviewer of boundary.pdf needs - and whether anything else in this family is still generated from one fixture and presented as if it described both.
